entries.proposition: Histoblots were taken at seven ages from P0 to P90 with three animals per group.
entries.snippet: For histoblotting, the animals used were from different litters and were grouped as follows: P0, P5, P10, P15, P21, P60 and P90 (n = 3 per group).

entries.proposition: The Figure 3 legend states that Cav3.1 expression increased progressively during postnatal development in the cerebellum and thalamus.
entries.snippet: This quantitative analysis indicates that Cav3.1 expression increased progressively during postnatal development in the Cb and Th.

entries.proposition: The Results text says the cerebellar molecular-layer Cav3.1 rose to a peak at P21 and decreased slightly at P60 and that the thalamus showed a similar pattern.
entries.snippet: However, in the ml of the Cb, the expression of Cav3.1 increased from its lowest expression at P0 to a peak at P21 and decreased slightly at P60 (Figures 3A,B). A similar developmental expression pattern was found in the Th (Figures 3A,B).
entries.anchor: Results, Expression Patterns of Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 During Postnatal Development

experimental_context.system: mouse brain histoblot densitometry, postnatal ages P0 to P60

entries.proposition: In the hippocampal subfields Cav3.2 was weak at P0, rose to a peak at P21 and decreased at P60.
entries.snippet: weak Cav3.2 expression was detected at P0, increased progressively to reach a peak at P21 and then decreased at P60

entries.proposition: The figure legend reports densitometry from four independent experiments averaged, a group description stated separately from the Methods group size.
entries.snippet: densitometric measurements from four independent experiments were averaged

entries.proposition: Antibody specificity for Cav3.2 was characterised with two wild-type and three Cav3.2-knockout mice.
entries.snippet: two wild-type and three Cav3.2-knockout mice (C57BL6/J strain) were used

entries.proposition: The animals studied run from the day of birth to adulthood in OF-1 mice.
entries.snippet: The OF-1 mice, from the day of birth [postnatal day (P0)] to adulthood

entries.proposition: Two anti-Cav3.3 antibodies failed to give an acceptable or specific signal, so this study reports no Cav3.3 result.
entries.snippet: Two different anti-Cav3.3 antibodies were also tested, but failed to provide an acceptable or specific signal.

entries.proposition: In the adult brain Cav3.1 immunoreactivity was strongest in the cerebellum and weaker in the thalamus, with faint staining in hippocampus, neocortex and septum.
entries.snippet: Immunoreactivity for Cav3.1 was strongest in the Cb and weaker in the thalamus (Th; Figures 1A,B). Faint staining was observed in the Hp, neocortex and septum (Sp; Figures 1A,B)
entries.anchor: Results, Differential Regional Expression, second paragraph

entries.proposition: In the adult brain Cav3.2 immunoreactivity was very strong in hippocampus, cerebellum, septum, caudate putamen and neocortex and moderate in the thalamus.
entries.snippet: Thus, very strong Cav3.2 immunoreactivity was observed in the Hp, Cb, Sp, CPu, and Cx, with moderate labeling in the Th
entries.anchor: Results, Differential Regional Expression, third paragraph

entries.proposition: For Cav3.2 the Results text reports a weak signal at P0, a progressive rise to a peak at P21 and a decrease at P60 in the hippocampal subfields.
entries.snippet: weak Cav3.2 expression was detected at P0, increased progressively to reach a peak at P21 and then decreased at P60 (Figures 4A,B)

entries.proposition: The authors state that to their knowledge this is the first detailed description of postnatal changes in T-type channel expression in the brain.
entries.snippet: To our knowledge, this data provide the first detailed description of the changes in T-type channel expression in the brain during postnatal development.
entries.anchor: Discussion, Differential Expression of Cav3.1 and Cav3.2 in the Adult and Developing Brain

entries.proposition: The authors report presynaptic Cav3.2 but not Cav3.1 labeling in axon terminals of excitatory synapses in hippocampus and cerebellum.
entries.snippet: we also found presynaptic labeling for Cav3.2 but not Cav3.1 channels in axon terminals establishing excitatory synapses in the Hp and Cb
